summary: Lower awaited fs/promises readFile to async C# I/O only when a JS-compatible Promise scheduler preserves fulfillment/rejection ordering.

requirements.usage: directly awaited or otherwise lowered through JS-compatible Promise machinery

semantics.return_value: Promise fulfillment with Buffer/string; rejection with Node-compatible error
semantics.abort_signal: supported; abort rejects with AbortError, while underlying OS requests may already have progressed
semantics.ordering: promise settlement must enter JS-compatible microtask scheduling

caveats: Task completion timing is not by itself ECMAScript Promise microtask semantics.
No encoding means Buffer, not string.

tests.name: await utf8 read
tests.expected_csharp: var s = await NodeFsPromises.ReadFileAsync(path, opts, jsPromiseScheduler);
tests.expected_behavior: await observes the decoded string or a Node-compatible rejection

tests.name: abort rejects
tests.input: const c=new AbortController(); const p=fsp.readFile('big',{signal:c.signal}); c.abort(); await p;
tests.expected_behavior: the promise rejects with an AbortError-compatible JS error when cancellation wins
